Combine the layers of a disturbance list that share a class name

Source: R/harmonizeList.R
harmonizeList.Rd

Within each sector of disturbances, layers with the same class name are combined into one layer with rbind(), unless the class name matches one of the patterns in whatNotToCombine.

Usage

harmonizeList(disturbances, whatNotToCombine = NULL)

Arguments

disturbances

A list of lists of SpatVectors, named by sector and then by class. A class name may appear more than once in a sector.

whatNotToCombine

Character vector of regular expressions. Classes whose name matches any of them are left as they are, repeats included. With NULL (the default), every repeated class is combined.

Value

A list with the sectors of disturbances. A sector with no class to combine is returned unchanged. In the others, the classes left as they are come first (those matching whatNotToCombine, then the rest), followed by the combined classes.

Author

Tati Micheletti, Ronald Kilian, Alex M. Chubaty

Examples

square <- function(x) {
  terra::vect(
    sprintf("POLYGON ((%1$d 0, %2$d 0, %2$d 1, %1$d 1, %1$d 0))", x, x + 1),
    crs = "EPSG:3857"
  )
}
disturbances <- list(
  mining = list(claims = square(0), claims = square(2), potentialMining = square(4))
)
out <- harmonizeList(disturbances, whatNotToCombine = "potential")
#> Harmonizing mining
#> Returning mining merged.
names(out$mining)
#> [1] "potentialMining" "claims"         
nrow(out$mining$claims)
#> [1] 2
